q: According to R. Yochanan, what kind of oath do the two holding a garment take?
options: A rabbinic ordinance, so people won't grab another's garment and claim it
A Torah oath of partial admission
why: It is a deterrent (*takkanat chakhamim*), which is why even Sumakhos can require it.

q: Two deposited 100 and 200 with one bailee, who forgot whose was whose; each claims 200. What do the Rabbis rule?
options: Each takes 100, and the disputed 100 is set aside until Elijah comes
The bailee pays both in full
All of it is set aside
why: R. Yosi sets aside the entire deposit, so the swindler loses too.

q: Why do the Rabbis divide the garment but set aside the disputed 100 dinars?
options: The garment may belong to both; the 100 surely belongs to only one
Only coins can be set aside
The garment was found, not deposited
why: If a split could be true, divide; if it would be patently false, set it aside.

q: Why doesn't R. Yosi set the garment aside, as he does the deposit?
options: Here it isn't certain anyone is lying: both may have lifted it together
Garments can't be held in court
why: The answer about the swindler's loss fails for a bought garment, so the 'no certain swindler' answer stands.

q: Storekeeper says he gave the laborer food; laborer says he got none. What happens?
options: Both swear and collect from the employer
The money is set aside until Elijah comes
why: Each deals only with the employer, who trusted both without witnesses, and he bears the loss.

q: R. Chiya: a claim of 100, a full denial, and witnesses to 50. What is the law?
options: He pays 50 and swears on the rest
why: By *kal va'chomer* from *modeh be'miktzat*: his own admission shouldn't weigh more than witnesses.

q: According to Rabba, why does the Torah impose an oath on one who admits part of a loan?
options: A debtor won't brazenly deny it all; he's stalling, and an oath can move him to admit
why: *Ein adam me'iz panav bifnei ba'al chovo*: he means to repay later, so an oath pushes him to admit everything.

q: In what respect is a litigant's own admission stronger than two witnesses, in a way the Gemara leaves unanswered?
options: It can't be contradicted or refuted by *hazamah*
why: Witnesses can be contradicted and refuted; an admission cannot. So the Gemara looks for another source.
